# Gauntlet Loop — Continuous Quality Backlog

Esta issue é a memória persistente do experimento de evolução incremental do Breakout por uma tarefa agendada do ChatGPT executada **de hora em hora**.

## Objetivo

Melhorar o jogo por ciclos pequenos, objetivos, verificáveis e reversíveis, preservando o escopo de HTML, CSS e JavaScript com Canvas 2D.

## Regra principal

> Cada execução deve implementar **exatamente uma melhoria** de maior impacto.

## Ordem de prioridade

1. Regressões e CI quebrado
2. Bugs de gameplay
3. Game feel
4. Controles e UX
5. Balanceamento e progressão
6. Acessibilidade e mobile
7. Performance
8. Polimento visual e áudio
9. Novas funcionalidades somente quando houver justificativa clara

## Ciclo esperado

1. Ler `main`, `README.md`, `GAUNTLET.md` e esta issue.
2. Ler comentários desta issue para entender o histórico dos ciclos anteriores.
3. Verificar o resultado disponível do CI/Playwright do commit mais recente.
4. Se houver regressão causada pelo último ciclo, corrigir essa regressão antes de qualquer melhoria nova.
5. Atuar como **CRITIC** e identificar o problema de maior impacto que caiba em uma alteração pequena e segura.
6. Atuar como **IMPLEMENTER** e implementar exatamente uma melhoria.
7. Adicionar ou atualizar testes relevantes.
8. Fazer commit diretamente em `main` somente quando a alteração estiver coerente e suficientemente validada.
9. Atuar como **JUDGE**: reavaliar se a mudança realmente melhora o jogo sem complexidade desnecessária.
10. Registrar nesta issue um comentário contendo problema, solução, commit, validações e observações para os próximos ciclos.

## Restrições

- Uma melhoria por execução.
- Não reescrever a arquitetura sem necessidade.
- Não adicionar dependências sem justificativa forte.
- Não ampliar arbitrariamente o escopo do jogo.
- Não sacrificar estabilidade por efeitos cosméticos.
- Preservar o baseline e a capacidade de comparar a evolução pelo histórico do Git.
- Usar Playwright/GitHub Actions como evidência objetiva sempre que aplicável.
- Se a evidência de CI ainda estiver pendente no fim de uma execução, registrar isso e deixar a próxima execução validar o resultado antes de iniciar uma nova melhoria.

## Baseline inicial

- Breakout simples em Canvas 2D
- 50 blocos
- 3 vidas
- pontuação
- controles por `←`, `→`, `A` e `D`
- sem framework de jogo
- Playwright e GitHub Actions configurados
- interface `window.__GAME_DEBUG__` disponível para testes

Esta issue deve permanecer aberta durante todo o experimento.
title: Gauntlet Loop — Continuous Quality Backlog

# **Arweave’s Perpetual Open Web Hackathon**

## **Introduction**

Welcome to the perpetual, open permaweb hackathon!

At Arweave we firmly believe that the future of the [new web should be open source](https://medium.com/@arweave/towards-an-open-source-web-9ffe201fc044) for the benefit of users and developers alike. We want to help make this a reality, so we’re rewarding developers like yourself for building open source dApps on the permaweb!

The Arweave itself is a global, permanent hard drive. The permaweb is a decentralised, immutable web built on top of the Arweave. Permaweb apps are built using normal web technologies — HTML, CSS, and Javascript — but are deployed to Arweave’s on-chain storage system, making them permanent and available in a fast, decentralised manner. You can get started and deploy a permaweb app in 2 minutes or less.

**Time investment:** One afternoon to one weekend.

**Please note that ALL submissions require approval via the [Discord Open Web Hackathon channel](https://discord.gg/ZdGZ8E29Sr).**

## **Reward**

**$250 in ETH + $50 in AR**
A dynamic and interactive web application that is hosted on the permaweb, along with ideas that contribute added functionality to the permaweb eco system. For example: [Arweave API explorer](https://arweave.net/LHff4F45o7ipDqjoePG0PDG5BD2hLD8xf17OBg4FjRE) & [ArweaveID](https://arweave.net/fGUdNmXFmflBMGI2f9vD7KzsrAc1s1USQgQLgAVT0W0). Ideas that resemble or improve on popular web applications such as [AskWeave](https://arweave.net/HhIjOjxgHYXJU5RVjRYfAR017vbZdujbCSlaA8NQ20U) & [Scribe](https://arweave.net/VOKAC_SYiUzbJrEaIY5SEBh1pf0bGQOd8c7G68nzet4#/) are also encouraged, and all applications must include a nice looking UI. Applications whose core features rely on centralised dependencies are not accepted. 

## **Resources**

You can find the docs for getting started deploying your first permaweb app [here](https://docs.arweave.org/developers/tools/textury-arkb).

The docs for the JS library that allows you to read from and write to the permaweb are [here](https://github.com/ArweaveTeam/arweave-js).

ArConnect wallet API docs can be found [here](https://docs.th8ta.org/arconnect/functions). 

Arweave.app wallet source files can be found [here](https://github.com/jfbeats/ArweaveWebWallet).

We’re providing some free tokens so you can get started building and deploying - grab your wallet [here](https://tokens.arweave.org/#/wallet). For guidance on how to use Arweave web wallets, check out [this user guide](https://docs.arweave.org/info/wallets/arweave-wallet).

## **Rules**

**[Check out ArweaveApps](http://arweaveapps.com) to ensure your submission is substantially different from existing applications on the permaweb!**

### **Successful submissions will meet the following criteria:**

- Submissions must be **your own original work**, and must be **unique or substantially different** from other permaweb applications or submissions to this hackathon
- We are happy to accept forks of other applications, but the featureset must be substantially different or significantly expanded in the forked version
Your app **_must_ interact with Arweave** using ArweaveJS
- Your app **must** include either [ArConnect](https://www.arconnect.io/) or [Arweave.app](https://arweave.app/) wallet integration - keyfile drag & drop login ***will not*** be accepted
- Apps must be **open source, with the full source code available on Github or another open code hosting repository**. Feel free to use whatever OSS licence you prefer
- Applications should be **sufficiently complex**, as judged by the core Arweave team. For example, a simple ‘hello world’ app is not complex enough to receive a reward. Broken/non-functional submissions will also be rejected. You should aim for a minimal viable product that an end-user could reasonably start to use
- Your submission must **include a link to a live, functioning, and running instance of the app itself, as well

> **Current scope — 2026-09-02:** Follow the [approved maintained-system alignment](https://github.com/richard-jh-mccrae/PokemonAI/issues/615#issuecomment-5515809745). It supersedes conflicting statements below and in earlier comments. Work is sequenced by real dependencies and quality requirements; no competition cutoff or post-submission phase applies.

---

Parent tracker: #600

### Phase

Post-submission.

### Depends on

- #611, #613, and preferably #614.
- Competition benchmark data from #609.

### Objective

Allocate search time according to decision difficulty and remaining match clock.

### Initial approach

Begin with an explicit rule-based controller using recorded search signals.

Later, train a budget model `B(s)` if data supports it.

### Candidate inputs

- remaining match time;
- turn number;
- branching factor;
- policy entropy;
- top-prior gap;
- top-`Q` gap;
- shallow/deep disagreement history;
- convergence rate;
- value uncertainty;
- chance-node count;
- game/prize leverage;
- forced/simple menu status.

### Scope

1. Define match-level budget accounting.
2. Guarantee a valid action before deadline.
3. Support:
   - near-zero search for obvious choices;
   - short search for normal choices;
   - deeper search for critical/uncertain turns.
4. Add stop/continue criteria based on expected improvement.
5. Record budget decisions and reasons.
6. Benchmark:
   - fixed per-decision budget;
   - fixed per-turn budget;
   - adaptive budget.
7. Train `B(s)` from convergence histories only after rule-based behavior is stable.
8. Enforce hard safety reserve for protocol/latency overhead.
9. Test worst-case high-branching matches.

### Acceptance criteria

- No evaluated match exceeds the configured hard search-time budget.
- Obvious decisions consume less search than difficult decisions.
- Adaptive budgeting improves or preserves strength at equal total match time.
- Budget decisions are reproducible in deterministic mode.
- Remaining-clock behavior is monotonic and safe.
- Search always returns a valid action on interruption.
- Learned budget work, if added, has a fixed-rule baseline.

### Out of scope

- Hidden-information multi-turn search.
- General cluster scheduling.

# Independent Review Queue

This issue is the **single review entrypoint** for the Second Brain repository.

Human shorthand command:

> `验算第二大脑`

The reviewer must NOT guess from “latest open PR”. This repository may have historical/frozen Draft PRs and multiple legitimate parallel engineering lines.

## Queue model: append-only exact-head tickets

Engineering posts `REVIEW_REQUEST/v1` only after a bounded slice reaches its independent-review stop gate. Ticket identity is `(pr, exact_head)`.

Reviewer appends `REVIEW_RESULT/v1` for that exact ticket:

```yaml
schema: REVIEW_RESULT/v1
project: SECOND_BRAIN
pr: <number>
reviewed_head: <sha>
verdict: ACCEPT | CHANGES_REQUIRED | BLOCKED
review_evidence_ref: <PR review/comment URL or id>
review_channel: GITHUB_APPROVE | EXACT_HEAD_COMMENT_ATTESTATION
reviewer_agent_id: GPT_INDEPENDENT_REVIEWER
independence_attestation: NO_PRODUCTION_CODE_OR_REMEDIATION_ON_REVIEWED_HEAD
```

A request is pending iff no later result exists for the exact same `(pr, exact_head)`. Remediation creates a new exact head and therefore a new request.

## Same-account GitHub APPROVE limitation

All ChatGPT engineering/reviewer windows currently operate through the same linked GitHub account. GitHub may reject a formal APPROVE with `Review Can not approve your own pull request`.

This platform limitation MUST NOT be bypassed or misrepresented.

When formal APPROVE is unavailable for this reason, the canonical independent-review evidence for our workflow is:

1. an exact-head PR review **COMMENT** containing the independent architecture/adversarial review;
2. a matching append-only `REVIEW_RESULT/v1` here with `verdict: ACCEPT` or `CHANGES_REQUIRED`;
3. exact `reviewed_head` equality with the current PR head at review completion;
4. reviewer role separation: the reviewing ChatGPT window did not implement or remediate the reviewed head;
5. fresh CI/current-main verification where required by the task.

1. Read this issue and all comments.

Every independent exact-head review MUST return all materially useful findings to the engineering/remediation path, regardless of verdict. An `ACCEPT` is not permission to discard non-blocking observations or future opportunities.

## Founder approval
Founder explicitly approved starting **HOSTED JENIFY HQ V1** on 2026-08-30 after PR #225 merged to `main` and post-merge CI passed.

## Starting point
Use fresh current `main`. The accepted local HQ foundation came through PR #225; merged commit observed at mission start: `85184a3be819fe1dede2f320cf43c6bad8603a6e`.

Do **not** reopen or rewrite PR #225. Build Hosted HQ as a new mission/branch/PR from fresh `main`.

## Why this mission exists
The current HQ control plane is proven to work on the Founder workstation, including:
- browser Direct Order creation
- distinct Founder approval / no-self-approval
- password step-up for Founder-gated work
- worker eligibility/check-only truth
- one real GitHub/Claude dispatch
- durable duplicate/retrigger refusal
- legitimate result ingest/correlation
- truthful live snapshot / Connection Center freshness

However the Vercel deployment is primarily a static/read-only preview. Navigation/rendering works, but the important controls are not a genuine hosted control plane. The Founder wants JENIFY HQ to be **actually usable online from phone/laptop**, not dependent on localhost for normal operation.

## Mission objective
Turn JENIFY HQ into a secure, genuinely functional **hosted control plane** while preserving the authority/security model already proven locally.

A Founder should be able to open the hosted HQ from an authorized browser and, when the hosted runtime is configured, safely:
1. sign in;
2. see current canonical HQ state;
3. create a Direct Order;
4. approve/deny Founder-gated work through a distinct authorized identity/session;
5. dispatch supported work without provider substitution;
6. see worker/task status update without rebuilding the static site;
7. receive and correlate legitimate results;
8. inspect live connection health;
9. use the core HQ experience from mobile as well as desktop.

## Product rule
Do **not** fake hosted functionality. A static/read-only deployment must say so. A live hosted control must only appear when its real authenticated backend capability exists.

## Architecture requirements
### 1. Hosted application/runtime
- Preserve the existing HQ application/Operator/Registry authority layers; hosted APIs must call the same canonical application logic rather than writing task/evidence tables directly.
- Replace the static-only operational experience with a real hosted data/API path where configured.
- Static build support may remain for fallback/docs/tests, but it must not masquerade as live.

### 2. Durable hosted state
The current local SQLite/workstation path is not enough for a multi-request hosted runtime.
- Design a durable hosted persistence adapter compatible with the current HQ store semantics.
- Preserve atomicity, idempotency, fencing, approval digest binding, dispatch evidence and audit history.
- Do not silently rely on ephemeral serverless filesystem state.
- Prefer the lowest-cost reliable architecture that satisfies the invariants.
- If choosing/activating a new external DB/cloud product requires a Founder credential, subscription, billing or irreversible service choice, finish all provider-neutral code/tests first and stop only at that explicit Founder gate with 2-3 concrete options, free/low-cost first.

### 3. Hosted Founder auth/security
Preserve and extend the proven browser security boundary:
- server-side authenticated sessions;
- explicit account -> HQ principal binding; never infer Founder authority from username/email;
- no-self-approval;
- step-up for Founder-gated/destructive approvals;
- trusted origin / CSRF protections appropriate for hosted HTTPS origins;
- HttpOnly/Secure/SameSite cookie behavior appropriate for public HTTPS hosting;
- fail closed when mapping/origin/config is absent;
- no secrets/tokens/private env values in HTML, JSON, browser bundle, logs, errors or evidence.

### 4. Live UI, not rebuild-driven UI
The current `UPDATED — page not rebuilt` behavior is truthful but not the hosted target

Follow-up to #4084 / #4085 (the agent demo skills: `react-native-ios-simulator`, `react-native-demo-screenshots`, `react-native-demo-videos`).

## Problem

Per-PR demo capture pays a repeated setup tax. Measured on a typical stills session (PR #4088 on-device proof, ~10 min wall-clock):

- Metro cold start + first bundle: **~2 min** (transform cache is per-worktree, so every PR starts cold)
- Each before/after flip: **~40 s** (terminate + launch + splash, since `initialRouteName` is only evaluated at mount)
- Sim claim + boot + app install: ~45 s
- Video sessions are far worse: a fresh staging login (OTP, coordinate taps, keyboard-overlay dismissal) adds several minutes per sim

## Proposed optimizations, by payoff

1. **Shared Metro transform cache for demo worktrees.** Point `cacheStores` at a stable `FileStore` (e.g. `~/.cache/metro-demo`) via a demo-only Metro config override. Successive PRs reuse transforms for unchanged files; first bundle should drop to ~15–30 s. Must not leak into the developer's own Metro config.
2. **Golden logged-in simulator, cloned per session.** Keep one blessed shutdown sim with the app installed and a staging account logged in; `claim-session.sh` clones it (`xcrun simctl clone`) instead of creating a blank device. Eliminates the login tax and the app install. Needs a staleness stamp (main SHA of the native build it carries) and a refresh rule.
3. **JS reload instead of cold relaunch for before/after flips.** The checkout-flip technique only changes JS, so a dev-server-triggered reload (Metro dev middleware / websocket) should replace terminate+launch+splash — ~35 s saved per flip, several flips per PR. Verify which reload endpoint the current RN version exposes.
4. **TTL bump / opt-in repo-scoped sim reuse.** `DEMO_SIM_TTL_HOURS=72` is free. A warm sim per repo (rather than per PR) saves boot+install but weakens per-PR isolation — only behind an explicit opt-in flag.

Explicitly rejected: parallel before/after on two simulators — it halves wall-clock but breaks the screenshots skill's same-device/same-state comparability rule.

## Constraints

The skill scripts carry test suites with a "new guarantee needs a failing assertion" rule (mutation-checked); each optimization should land as a small, tested patch, in payoff order: Metro cache → reload flip → golden-sim clone → TTL/opt-in reuse.
title: task(agents): Speed up simulator demo capture between PRs (skills follow-up to #4085)

## Priority

**Setup-critical.** The immediate goal is to make the existing production label system reliable enough that normal printing failures do not create PostgreSQL cleanup work during Setup preparation.

This issue intentionally stays focused on the **existing LabelPrintService + Directus boolean workflow** while making the design forward-compatible with additional label sizes, printers, and a future Label Printing application.

## Current production baseline

The current workflow remains in place for this phase:

```text
Directus

LabelPrintService
    -> polls PostgreSQL
    -> determines pending work
    -> preflight
    -> creates snapshot batch
    -> prints
    -> finalizes / clears print_label after success
```

There is no requirement in this issue to replace the boolean request path with a new application or request table before Setup.

## Immediate problems to solve

### 1. Preflight is incomplete

Live recovery on 2026-08-27 proved that the current service can pass printer/template checks, create/commit a batch, and then fail on a missing runtime path. That leaves a FAILED batch and requires manual PostgreSQL cleanup before printing can resume.

**Required rule:**

> If full preflight does not pass, PostgreSQL execution-batch state must remain unchanged.

For the current pending workload, preflight must validate every deterministic prerequisite before batch creation, including at minimum:

- required SQL files exist/readable;
- configured runtime CSV/output paths exist or can be safely created;
- output paths are writable without destroying an existing file;
- selected template exists and b-PAC can open it;
- selected Windows printer can be used;
- loaded media is present and matches the selected label requirement;
- Windows print queue is in a safe state;
- required runtime/log/state directories are valid;
- no conflicting active/failed batch prevents safe execution.

`write_csv()` should still defensively create its parent directory immediately before writing, but that is race protection, not a substitute for preflight.

### 2. The service cannot distinguish two Display label sizes

MSB now has a confirmed need for at least two Display identity label formats on the PT-P950NW:

```text

Display identity — narrow format: 24 mm (1-inch nominal) laminated tape
```

The current Python service assumes one Displ

# 🤖 Claude Coordination Board

Live cross-session comms for parallel Claude sessions. **Standing/pinned, never closed.**

## ⚠️ POST WITH `add_issue_comment`. `issue_write method=update` DESTROYS THIS BODY.

`issue_write method=update` is the **edit-the-issue** tool, not the comment tool. The comment tool is **`add_issue_comment`**.

**Why it keeps recurring, and why a careful reader still hits it:**

- **The MCP's return value is indistinguishable from a successful comment.** Both return an id and a URL. Nothing errors, nothing warns — the session moves on believing it posted, and the damage is found later by someone else. *(This is exactly how the 2026-08-29 clobber went unnoticed until the next read.)*
- **Instructions that say "post a comment" without naming the tool leave the choice to inference**, and `issue_write` is the plausible-looking guess for "write to an issue".
- **Nothing enforces it.** `.claude/settings.json` hooks are inert on Claude Code on the web (`BL-20260820-PROJECT-HOOKS-INERT-ON-WEB`), so this is self-discipline.

**Recorded clobbers (8):** 2026-07-30 · 2026-08-09 · 2026-08-15 · 2026-08-19 · 2026-08-20 08:52Z · 2026-08-20 08:56Z (four minutes apart, two sessions neither of which could see the other) · 2026-08-23 18:13Z · **2026-08-29 17:59Z (this one)**.

**If you clobber it anyway:** say so on the board immediately, restore from `docs/claude/coordination-board.md`, and **label the result a reconstruction** — do not pass a rebuild off as the original. When restoring, note that **GitHub strips `<…>` as HTML even inside code fences**, so use `{braces}` in the body.

## Why this board exists

Multiple Claude sessions run in parallel and **still collide** even with the merge queue. `docs/claude/session-board.json` + branch protection serialize only the *one merge slot*; they do nothing to stop two sessions editing the same file, redoing the same workstream blind to each other, or blocking on a question only another live session can answer. A committed file propagates only through a merge + pull — too late. **An issue's comments are visible to every session immediately.** That is the board.

# Autonomous roadmap — stabilize core before scaling

The product is still in test mode with only part of the future manager/source pool connected. Immediate goal: remove software/state/routing/notification/dialogue defects and simplify the architecture so adding managers and traffic later does not multiply edge cases.

## Autopilot rules
- Prioritize real live conversations, handoffs and user requests over commit history.
- Confirm a defect from evidence where possible; otherwise add diagnostics/tests first.
- Safe reversible flow: branch → PR → required CI → merge only when green → verify production SHA, migrations, smoke/health and relevant live behavior.
- Do not make unrelated changes or edit other AnyTour projects from this roadmap.
- Do not silently enable off-shift managers, auto-assign conversations or add aggressive SLA escalation during test mode.
- Stop only for irreversible/high-risk decisions, missing secrets/credentials or unresolved product decisions.
- Prefer eliminating a class of bugs over adding another one-off guard when repeated live evidence points to the same architectural weakness.

# Milestone 1 — Dialogue Core Stabilization
Goal: make dirty input, repeated callbacks and natural text predictable before scaling traffic.

## 1A. Interaction safety
- [x] Existing live fixes for stale/concurrent date, month, forward wizard and edit-menu callbacks (#88/#102/#103/#109/#113).
- [x] Shared `InteractionGuard` foundation (#114): callback lock paths, duplicate-window checks, recent-burst checks and forward-step expectations are centralized without changing current behavior.
- [x] Structured callback suppression diagnostics foundation (#116): current guarded stale/duplicate/concurrent paths emit `interaction_guard / callback_suppressed` with reason, scope and canonical current/expected state where known; legacy text logs remain for compatibility.
- [x] Unknown callback fallback now uses the same structured suppression channel (#118): valid non-empty callbacks with no owning action emit reason `unknown_action`, scope `callback_controller`, payload and chat id while preserving the existing unhandled return behavior.
- [ ] Move remaining callback-safety decisions behind the shared guard instead of adding per-action lock/debounce implementations.
- [ ] Add callback generation/version support so buttons rendered by an older interaction can be rejected generically after state changes.
- [ ] Extend structured suppression reason to obsolete generation once that path exists.
- [ ] Verify intentional back/edit/reopen actions are not incorrectly suppressed.

## 1B. Formal dialogue state machine
- [x] Canonical wizard states and forward/back/edit/reset transition rules are defined in `DialogueStateMachine` (#115), including conditional child-age flow and current AI missing-field behavior.
- [x] Forward callback status expectations in `InteractionGuard` now resolve through the canonical state machine instead of a duplicate status map (#115).
- [x] Observe-first diagnostics are live on guarded invalid forward/date/month callback attempts (#116), without introducing any new blocking semantics.
- [x] Explicit edit-flow state preservation foundation from live conversation 311 (#122): edit completion restores missing unchanged values from a snapshot while the edited value remains authoritative and reset clears the snapshot.
- [x] Root cause missed by #122 fixed from the next natural production edit (#124): the full trip snapshot is now captured when `edit_params` opens, **before** `EditParamsView::menu()` appends another check/status boundary; concrete `edit_x` selection reuses that pre-menu snapshot. This directly addresses the reproduced `edit_country → Китай → empty check summary` path.
- [x] City edit completion fixed from live conversation 356 (#128): `edit_params → edit_city → pick_city_*` now finishes the `city` edit through `EditFlowService` and returns to the preserved check summary instead of incorrectly continuing into

body_excerpt:
### 赏金平台 / Platform
GitHub

### 原始链接 / Source URL
https://github.com/tenstorrent/tt-metal/issues/54551

### 漏洞描述 / Description
[Bounty $1,000] ttnn.prod_bw returns non-finite gradients for zero inputs

## Summary

`ttnn.prod_bw` computes the gradient as

```text
prod(input) * grad / input
```

which is `reciprocal(input)` multiplied by a broadcast `prod(input) * grad`. Where the input
contains an exact zero, `reciprocal(0)` is `+inf` and the surviving product is `0`, so the
gradient at that position is non-finite instead of the finite value autograd defines.

```text
input:    [2, 0, 4]
grad:     1
expected: [0, 8, 0]
current:  [0, non-finite, 0]
```

This is a source-level analysis: I do not have a card, so the host replay below renders the
device `inf * 0` as a non-finite value without asserting which one appears in silicon. The defect
is that the gradient is non-finite where the correct value is finite.

## Root cause

Both branches multiply by `reciprocal(input)`:

- `dim=None`:
  [`unary_backward.cpp#L1668-L1676`](https://github.com/tenstorrent/tt-metal/blob/a5cd86212e/ttnn/cpp/ttnn/operations/eltwise/unary_backward/unary_backward.cpp#L1668-L1676)
  — `multiply(reciprocal(input), fill_first_val_into_tensor(prod * grad))`.
- per-dimension: `reciprocal_input` is built once at
  [`L1711`](https://github.com/tenstorrent/tt-metal/blob/a5cd86212e/ttnn/cpp/ttnn/operations/eltwise/unary_backward/unary_backward.cpp#L1711)
  and feeds every `dim` branch, e.g. `dim=-1` at
  [`L1722`](https://github.com/tenstorrent/tt-metal/blob/a5cd86212e/ttnn/cpp/ttnn/operations/eltwise/unary_backward/unary_backward.cpp#L1722).
  All four dimensions are affected, not only `dim=-1`.

At a zero input the product of the other values has already been lost in the reduction, so it
cannot be recovered by the division. The formula is valid only when the reduced input has no zeros.

## Reproducer

Host only, no device required (`pip install torch`):

```python
"""Source-level replay of ttnn.prod_bw against torch.prod autograd.

Replays the composite expression from tt-metal main @ a5cd86212e. Runs on host only:
it does not need a Tenstorrent device.
"""

import math
import torch


def source_pr

## Demonstrated current-main gap
Current main `62c6435011cc11e2c38ff146f187518fb9641fff` registers `auction` in `CANONICAL_NORMAL_EVENT_IDS` and leaves it selectable; `resolveCanonicalNormalEvent('auction', ...)` delegates to existing `resolveAuctionEvent` in `runtime/mapless-auction-flow.js`.

The production generic Safari handoff `runtime/safari-normal-event-touch-handoff.js` does not include `auction` in `SUPPORTED`, and `normal-event-touch-presentation.js` has no `auction` owner module/action resolver. There is no `runtime/safari-auction-interaction.js` at current main, and the root production presentation inventory has no auction sidecar. Therefore a selectable Board auction has canonical resolution truth but no demonstrated Safari/Web interaction path.

## Required implementation
- First validate the v0.9.108 auction choices/ordering/price and product-generation contract against canonical cache/artifact; do not guess missing Ruby behavior.
- Reuse `resolveCanonicalNormalEvent('auction', ...)` / `resolveAuctionEvent`; do not copy auction mechanics into presentation.
- Reuse existing Bag/economy transaction and Board/Persistence owners. Money/product grant and Board consumption must be atomic/exactly once.

Sub-issue 1 of 5 under #378, which records the defect and its measurement but
prescribes no fix. This one carries the fix.

## Goal

**Today.** `globToRegExp` (`src/inspect/filter.ts`) never returns when its glob
holds a `{` with no `}` after the cursor. In the `{` branch, `glob.indexOf('}', i)`
answers `-1`; `i = end` puts the cursor at `-1`; the `for` loop's `i++` moves it to
`0`; the scan restarts from the front of the glob with `pattern` one whole segment
longer than the pass before. Nothing in the loop can reach the exit condition, so
the string grows until V8 aborts on heap exhaustion.

The adopter gets no blueprint error — nothing names the glob, the config field, or
the `.gitignore` line it came from. What they see is the command sitting there and
then V8's own `<--- Last few GCs --->` block and
`FATAL ERROR: Ineffective mark-compacts near heap limit Allocation failed - JavaScript heap out of memory`.
How long the wait is scales with the heap ceiling — a couple of seconds at
`--max-old-space-size=128`, tens of seconds at 1024 — so at a default Node old
space it is minutes, not seconds. (Exact timings are machine-dependent and vary by
more than 50% between runs; the ordering is the point, not the numbers.)

**Wanted.** An unmatched `{` compiles as a literal `{`, the function returns, and
the caller gets a pattern that matches a path spelled with a literal brace. No
balanced glob changes.

**And — added by the owner after stage 1 landed — the adopter is told.** Stage 1
turned a crash into a silence, and for two of the four fields that silence is worse
than the crash was, because it reads as success. Measured during delivery:

- **`testFiles` produces a wrong green.** `unavailableGate` keys on
  `testFiles.length === 0`, not on how many files the globs resolve to. So
  `testFiles: []` reports `· declared, unavailable here testFilename` with its cause
  spelled out, while `testFiles: ['**/*.test.{ts']` reports `✓ error testFilename`
  and `1/16 optional gates active` — **byte-identical to a healthy config**, for a
  gate real ESLint then applies to zero files.

  **The diagnosis here stands and the remedy it implies does not — stage 15 replaced
  it.** Byte-identical output *was* the defect. **Closing the gate was the wrong
  repair**: the rule is genuinely emitted beside a `files` holding that glob, so the
  gate is armed and reporting it shut is a wrong red. Stage 2 kept the diagnosis and
  closed an open gate; **stage 15 kept the diagnosis and named the entry instead.**
  Left in place rather than rewritten, because the reasoning that produced the wrong
  remedy is worth more to the next reader than a clean-looking paragraph. The same broken glob stops
  `dropTestFiles` exempting anything, so `inspect` begins reporting findings
  **against test files** and exits non-zero, with the offending glob appearing
  nowhere in the output. `docs/guide/reference.md` meanwhile publishes *"Test files
  (`architecture.testFiles`) are exempt throughout."*
- **`layerFilesIgnore` is silent outright.** With eslint wired so `wiringCheck`
  runs, `doctor`'s output is byte-identical between a correct ignore glob and a
  broken one — banner and exit code included. It is not a net, so `outsideNets` and
  the vacuous line cannot reach it even in principle.

`layerFiles` is the one field the existing surface does cover, and #381's constraint
3 is written so that coverage survives. These two are not covered by #381 or by any
other sibling.

**What the gap costs.** Four adopter-reachable inputs feed this function with no
check in front of them, across four commands:

- **A root `.gitignore` line → `blueprint init`.** `toRule`
  (`src/bootstrap/ignored.ts`) compiles every line that survives its own trimming and
  `!` / trailing-slash handling through `globToRegExp`. Git's own ignore syntax has no brace expansion, so a `{` there is
  an ordinary path c
title: A stray `{` in an adopter's glob compiles literally, instead of hanging the command

## Purpose

This issue is the durable coordination, queue, lease, recovery and handoff point for Dungeon Veil autonomous work. GitHub is the source of truth. Chat reports are informational only. Replit is forbidden.

## Active operating model: exactly two regular workers

Dungeon Veil uses exactly two regular ChatGPT automation roles in `Europe/Berlin`. Their actual enabled schedules are external automation state and must be read live; do not hard-code clock times here or infer them from historical comments.

1. **Master implementer** (`worker: primary`)
   - owns the highest-priority free product task;
   - implements, tests, commits, pushes and maintains its PR;
   - creates a risk-based exact-head test plan and inspects the selected evidence;
   - may carry a fully accepted exact head through Ready, merge and publication.
2. **Master verifier** (`worker: verifier`)
   - independently verifies the risk classification, test-plan mapping, exact-head gates, reviews, threads and evidence;
   - expands an understated plan and may safely fix focused defects when no primary scope overlaps;
   - performs final acceptance, Expected-Head merge without auto-merge, retains branches and verifies deployment.

The actual enabled automation configuration is authoritative for execution times. If repository text and live automation state disagree only about schedule, correct the stale documentation; do not change worker scope or create an extra regular worker just to match an old clock time.

There are no active scheduled `secondary` or `visual` workers. Old comments using those worker names are historical records only and do not authorize new work. Do not create additional regular workers unless the user explicitly changes this operating model after concrete evidence that two workers are insufficient.

`worker: background` is permitted only for an explicitly separate, short-lived coordination or migration task. It is never a third scheduled product worker.

## Immutable project rules

- repository: `ys2mm422yb-max/DungeonVeil`
- only target, test and publication branch: `fix/mobile-telegraphs-room-21-50-balance`
- only public test URL: `https://ys2mm422yb-max.github.io/DungeonVeil/`
- never change, target, merge into or publish from `main`
- leave PR #315 untouched
- no auto-merge
- no automatic branch deletion
- no force-push, reset or overwriting another worker's commits
- Playwright retries remain `0`
- do not weaken assertions, coverage, thresholds, acceptance criteria or timeouts
- evidence follows Issue #366 budgets and SHA-256 deduplication
- no temporary GitHub Actions workflows as patch transport

A known defect, rejecting user report, unresolved review requirement, unreviewed visual issue or unmet acceptance criterion blocks Ready and merge.

## Mandatory work order and state machines

Finish existing priority work before opening unnecessary new PRs. Current order is maintained in the newest handoffs below.

Primary state machine:
`IMPLEMENTIEREN -> TESTPLAN -> EXAKT-HEAD-TESTS -> EVIDENCE -> READY -> READY-GATES -> MERGE -> DEPLOY -> DONE`

Verifier state machine:
`VERIFY -> TESTPLAN-REVIEW -> EVIDENCE -> READY-GATES -> MERGE -> DEPLOY -> DONE`

A worker may not report the same exact head, state and blocker for three consecutive runs without a new concrete action. `waiting_external` is not a run-ending condition when independent work is available.

## Live queue discovery

At the start of every pass read this issue and its newest comments, `AGENTS.md`, `docs/ADAPTIVE_TEST_POLICY.md`, roadmap #323, open issues, PRs, reviews, exact-head Actions, artifacts, deployments and current user feedback.

Queue priority:

1. safety, data loss, auth, build, deployment and merge blockers;
2. current exact-head red, cancelled or missing gates;
3. unresolved reviews, active PR defects and rejected user feedback;
4. unfinished acceptance criteria in existing work;
5. visible UI/gameplay/mobile/asset defects

## Zweck

Dauerhafter Betriebs- und Self-Healing-Vertrag für Dungeon Veil. GitHub und das produktive Supabase-Projekt müssen nicht nur bei Feature-Arbeit, sondern kontinuierlich durch die bestehenden zwei regulären Autopiloten (`primary`, `verifier`) gepflegt, auf Drift geprüft und bei sicheren, belegten Abweichungen selbstständig repariert werden.

**Einziges Supabase-Projekt:** `hfndwqfghyomwapqsked`. DokoHilf `efifbuqctylsujiauabg` ist strikt ausgeschlossen.

## Definition von „alles automatisch pflegen“

### 1. GitHub Source-of-Truth und Repository-Hygiene
Bei jedem Lauf mindestens den veränderlichen Live-Zustand berücksichtigen und bei relevanter Änderung erneut prüfen:
- Zielbranch-Head `fix/mobile-telegraphs-room-21-50-balance`
- #376-Leases/Handoffs, Roadmap #323, aktive/relevante Issues
- offene/Draft/Ready/parked PRs, Base/Head/Drift/Mergeability
- Reviews und Review-Threads
- Exact-Head Actions inklusive relevante rote/abgebrochene/fehlende Gates
- Artefakte/Evidence, Deployment-Receipts und GitHub Pages
- stale/inkonsistente PR-/Issue-/Roadmap-Metadaten
- Workflow-/Validator-/Evidence-Drift und wiederkehrende Infrastrukturfehler

Keine Wartung darf `main`, PR #315, Auto-Merge, Branch-Autodelete, Force-Push/Reset oder Acceptance/Test-Abschwächung einführen.

### 2. Supabase Live-State und Repo-Drift
Kontinuierlich den produktiven Live-Stand mit dem Repository abgleichen:
- Projektstatus/Region/Postgres-Version
- `supabase/migrations/**` gegen produktive Migration-History und tatsächliche Objekte
- Tabellen, RLS, Policies, direkte Grants, Sequenzen und Publications
- RPCs/Funktionen, besonders `SECURITY DEFINER`
- Edge Functions live gegen `supabase/functions/**`, Status und `verify_jwt`
- Realtime-/Auth-/Postgres-/API-/Edge-Logs bei Fehlern oder betroffenen Änderungen
- Cron/Scheduler/Worldboss-Rotation und andere serverseitige Zeitverträge
- Schema-/Type-/Function-Drift, wenn relevant

Repo ist die deklarative Quelle. Keine stillen manuellen Produktionsänderungen. Datenbank-/Function-Änderungen müssen aus bereits versioniertem Repository-Stand stammen oder zuerst als fokussierte Migration/Function-Änderung über GitHub dokumentiert werden.

### 3. Security-Baseline
Neue oder veränderte Backend-Flächen sind mindestens auf Folgendes zu prüfen:
- Least privilege; `anon`/`public` nur wenn ausdrücklich erforderlich
- RLS für benutzerbezogene bzw. sensible Tabellen
- minimale direkte Table-Grants; RPC-only-Flächen ausdrücklich dokumentieren
- `SECURITY DEFINER` nur wenn technisch nötig, mit fixer `search_path`, expliziter Auth-/Autorisierungsprüfung und sicherer Objektauflösung
- keine unbeabsichtigte `anon`/`public`-EXECUTE-Freigabe
- Edge Functions standardmäßig `verify_jwt=true`, außer ein bewusst dokumentierter externer Webhook erfordert etwas anderes
- Service-Role/Secrets niemals in Repository, Issues, PRs oder Logs veröffentlichen
- Auth-Sicherheitsoptionen wie Leaked-Password-Protection als echte Plattformkonfiguration prüfen; wenn nicht direkt automatisierbar, als offener Security-Punkt tracken bis technisch geklärt bzw. nachweislich nicht anwendbar

Supabase Advisor-Meldungen werden **klassifiziert**, nicht blind „auf Null“ repariert:
- `actionable`: echte Schwäche/Drift -> beheben und verifizieren
- `intentional-controlled`: bewusstes Design (z. B. RPC-only Tabelle ohne direkte Grants) -> dauerhafte Begründung/Baseline
- `unknown/new`: untersuchen; neue unerklärte WARN/ERROR ist Wartungsarbeit und kann je nach Risiko Produktarbeit preempten

### 4. Performance-Baseline
- fehlende FK-Indizes prüfen und bei realer/absehbarer Relevanz sicher ergänzen
- Slow/Error-Logs bei relevanten Symptomen prüfen
- Advisor `unused_index` niemals allein als Grund zum Löschen verwenden; erst Query-/Nutzungsbeleg und sichere Regression-/Rollback-Strategie
- keine Performance-„Optimierung“ auf Kosten von RLS, Idempotenz, Exactly-once oder Datenintegrität

### 5. Produktionsänderungen
Backend-/Auth-/RLS-/RPC-/Realtime-/Persistenz-/C
title: Autonomous stewardship: keep GitHub and Supabase continuously secure, synchronized and healthy

## Goal
Build the **first actually playable web version of 《생존일기》** by reusing the existing Web Play Shell, M0 play UI parts, Validator/Action Queue, Canon v2, and AI GM roadmap.

Target experience:
> A player can open the web app, read the current scene, see minimal family/current state, choose a numbered action or enter a free action, advance a turn, see the result/log, and continue for a short real play session.

This is **not** a full product. It is a 10–20 turn playable MVP proving that the core ChatGPT play experience can live inside the web shell.

## Planning approval
The planning room approved this implementation direction on 2026-09-01.

Human-approved architecture decisions for this Issue:
- Canon v2 is authoritative for the new web MVP.
- Legacy `players/main/RUNTIME_STATE.json` / `core/CHARACTERS.json` must not be treated as Canon v2 current truth.
- Raw Transcript is cold archive only and must never be loaded by the normal runtime.
- Keep the architecture invariant: **AI proposes/interprets, engine validates/commits.**
- Reuse existing code; do not restart the web game from scratch.

This Issue is therefore the current implementation Source of Truth under `engine/AGENTS.md` when it conflicts with stale older active-development notes.

## Existing assets to reuse
Do not duplicate these unless necessary:
- `engine/web` React + TypeScript + Vite shell
- current `StateConsole`, `PlayBridge`, BGM controls
- existing `SceneHeader`, `ChoiceButtons`, `FreeActionForm`, `GameLog`, status components
- existing state/controller/validator/action-queue implementation
- existing M0/M1/M2 regression coverage
- closed Zero-AI vertical-slice PR #14 as a **reference implementation only** for turn loop, ordered actions, local save, family/world behavior; do not revive Zero-AI as the primary architecture
- Issue #42 AI GM Web Runtime roadmap
- Issue #43 / Draft PR #44 AI GM structured-action benchmark work

## Phase 1 — Canon v2 Runtime Bridge
### Required
Create a thin, explicit Canon v2 runtime/view adapter for the web app.

It must use the current Canon v2 boot/state sources appropriate for the active season, including the current `REBOOT_START_HERE.md` rules.

For the first implementation target, support the latest prepared Canon v2 continuation state rather than Legacy current state.

### Hard boundaries
- Do not load `seasons_v2/**/raw_transcript/**` or any Raw Transcript content.
- Do not silently fall back to Legacy `players/main/RUNTIME_STATE.json` / `core/CHARACTERS.json` as Canon v2 truth.
- Do not expose Hidden World Seed / GM-only state in public browser payloads.
- If the Canon v2 source set is insufficient to construct a machine-readable public runtime safely, stop with `BLOCKED / HUMAN DECISION NEEDED` and identify the smallest missing contract rather than inventing Canon facts.

### MVP public view
Expose only what the player needs:
- season / phase
- date / time / location
- family: name/relationship, location, simple visible condition/status
- key resources
- current base / visible facility capabilities
- active visible pressure/problem
- recent visible change
- checkpoint/source status

## Phase 2 — Restore playable scene loop in the existing web shell
Turn the current read-only-first shell into a playable MUD screen without removing useful State Console data.

Minimum flow:
1. current text scene
2. minimal family/current state
3. numbered choices
4. free-action input
5. submit action
6. advance turn
7. show resulting scene/state
8. append turn log

Reuse existing components and prior M0/PR #14 patterns where appropriate.

### Interaction requirements
- numbered choices must be keyboard/touch friendly
- free action must use normal text input on mobile
- preserve ordered multi-action support where the existing action queue can already support it safely
- no forced numeric keypad for compound action text
- family are not direct player-controlled units; requests may be accepted, modified, delayed, or refused by famil

## Mission

This is the **umbrella implementation / computation / paper-closure issue** for the major V2 update introduced by #48 and #49.

The goal is not to memorialize a few famous discoveries. The goal is to make ORION-V2 capable of studying **scientific development itself**: very large populations of successful, failed, partial, redirected and abandoned research trajectories; the conceptual/formal/experimental moves inside them; the conditions under which those moves help or fail; and recursively higher-order principles that survive held-out fields, epochs, problems and prospective tests.

> ORION should learn increasingly general principles of how knowledge develops, while preserving native science, mathematics, counterexamples, negative results, resource costs and reopen conditions. No level is accepted merely because it is elegant or more abstract.

At issue creation the active branch was `research/wave6-contraction-closure-20260827` at `391ac51f8b1df047650df575877b84b7dac76b14`. **Always fetch latest head and latest #45/#46/#47/#48/#49 before acting.** Do not overwrite concurrent execution work.

---

## Governing issues and non-negotiable rules

- #45 — outcome-generating execution/computation master.
- #46 — scientificity / sceptical-review gate.
- #47 — adaptive mechanism/theory revision gate.
- #48 — open-world conceptual development, transfer discovery, mathematical formal mechanics and formalism genesis.
- #49 — population-scale recursive science of scientific development.
- #38 — external field/name demarcation.
- #8 / #37 — V1/V2 parity and independent custody.

Scientific rules:

1. `NEW_VOCABULARY != NEW_SCIENCE`.
2. `RIGOUR_PROCESS != SCIENTIFIC_TRUTH`.
3. Same-model critique/repeated seeds are not independent replication.
4. Never hide parent wins, simple-control wins, ties, adverse results, invalid tasks or `CANNOT_CHECK`.
5. Never change frozen confirmatory endpoints after outcome access. A legitimate repair/revision gets a new prospective identity.
6. Strongest applicable mathematical/scientific parent is always a real comparator, never a strawman.
7. Formal proof/consistency cannot substitute for empirical evidence; empirical success cannot substitute for a mathematical witness when a formal claim is made.
8. No internal run self-grants field status, journal acceptance, R4, or universal law status.

---

# A. Finish the V2 framework as one coherent hierarchy

The framework should no longer look like a pile of modules. Integrate the following levels with explicit interfaces, inputs, outputs, receipts, parent owners, ablations and kill conditions.

### L0 — scientific episode / scientific-state transition

A bounded episode contains problem/frame, scientific state, obligations, sources/evidence, models/computation, uncertainty, actions/resources, validation/oracles, history and authority.

A scientific transition changes a commitment, representation, method, problem, experiment, source/evaluator state or agenda and returns an auditable receipt.

### L1 — knowledge metabolism

Discover/decompose/sort/native-reconstruct/reduce/absorb/recombine/challenge/assimilate-or-recycle knowledge while preserving provenance, assumptions, counterexamples, dependence and authority.

### L2 — transfer discovery

Do **not** hard-code physics/math/science lessons. Learn candidate reusable structure from source-bound donors:

`encounter -> structural description -> candidate discovery -> alignment -> bounded projection -> native recovery -> negative-transfer challenge -> hidden evaluation -> memory update`.

Support math→math, math→science, science→math/formalization and science→science.

### L3 — conceptual development

Version concepts as states, not labels. Support typed transitions such as `SPECIALIZE`, `GENERALIZE`, `SPLIT`, `MERGE`, `BRIDGE`, `REPARAMETERIZE`, `REVISE`, `DEPRECATE`.

A conceptual change needs predecessor/native recovery, explicit scope/loss, preserved old-valid cases, operational links, falsifiers and

**Area:** `@theokit/agents` — `bridge/define-agent.ts`, `bridge/sdk-adapter-create-options.ts` ·
**Severity:** medium (a capability the SDK offers is unreachable through the documented layer)
**Build under test:** `@theokit/agents@12.1.0`, `@theokit/sdk@4.52.1` installed, `4.63.3` latest

Raised by the TheoCode session after verifying the SDK's `#524` opt-in against a real consumer
through a pkg.pr.new preview. The verification is theirs and it is sound; the framing here adds one
measurement that changes what can be done about it today.

## The gap

`compatSources` — the SDK's opt-in that re-enables `.claude/` discovery after the default became
`.theokit`-only — has **no forward in this layer**. A product that is forbidden from importing
`@theokit/sdk` directly, which is the documented arrangement, therefore has no line to write.

The new default is the right one and was asked for: a directory holding only `.claude/` used to
yield `leaked-skill / analyst / leaked-agent` and execute a planted PreToolUse hook; on the SDK
preview it yields `analyst` alone and the hook does not run (measured by TheoCode, consumer suite
green: 94 files / 753 tests). What is missing is the escape hatch for someone whose `.claude/` hooks
are legitimately theirs.

## What blocks the fix today, and this is the part worth knowing before anyone starts

**`compatSources` is not in any published version of `@theokit/sdk`.** Measured 2026-09-02 by
unpacking the tarballs:

| Version | `compatSources` | `settingSources` (positive control) |
|---|---|---|
| `4.52.1` (installed here) | absent | present |
| `4.63.3` (`latest`) | absent | present |
| `4.63.4-next.0` (`next`) | absent, across 490 `.d.ts` | present |

It exists only in the SDK commit behind the preview. So a forward written now could not be typed
against an installable version, could not be tested, and — worse — would be **silently inert**:
`sdk-adapter-create-options.ts` hands `local` to `Agent.create`, and an SDK that does not know the
key ignores it. A consumer would declare the opt-in, pass this layer's gate, and get nothing. That is
the fabricated-mechanism failure this repository spends most of its gates preventing.

**This issue is therefore blocked on the SDK publishing `compatSources`**, and says so rather than
sitting in a backlog looking actionable.

## The shape it should take when unblocked

Not a raw pass-through. `settingSources` already refuses to be one, for a reason that applies here
more sharply (`bridge/setting-sources-gate.ts`):

- `'project'` authorises `<cwd>/.theokit/hooks.json`, **which executes shell**, so the API takes a
  `ProjectSettingsGrant` carrying a `TrustPosture` rather than a string. Evidence, not a claim.
- `compatSources: ['claude-code']` authorises `<cwd>/.claude/hooks.json` — the same shell execution,
  on a directory that is even more likely to have arrived with a cloned repository.

So it wants the same asymmetry the existing selection has: a root the operator owns needs no gate; a
root whoever wrote the repository controls needs a posture. Something like a `claudeCode?:
ProjectSettingsGrant` member on the existing selection, resolved through the same
`resolveSettingSources` path, rather than a second vocabulary beside it.

**One SDK behaviour the gate must not break** (noted by TheoCode): an unrecognised source name is
DROPPED upstream, not turned into `<cwd>/<name>` — a typo fails closed. Whatever this layer adds
must not turn that into a throw, or a mistyped source becomes a crash instead of a safe default.

## Verification available

TheoCode offered the method that found this: preview pin, real TUI, resumed session with a tool
call. That same method already caught something the SDK's own tests did not — that the `#523` fix
recovers an already-poisoned session rather than only preventing new ones, confirmed against a real
transcript carrying 7 markers.

---
*Filed from the theokit session; the measurement of what is published is mine, the end-to-end
ver
title: agents: compatSources has no forward, so a consumer on this layer cannot opt into .claude discovery at all — and the forward cannot be built yet

Tracking issue for making Recoup Chat the simplest way for anyone to create a music video: one conversation that produces the song, the visuals, and the finished cut, playable in the thread. Every building block already exists in `api` (music generation, six video modes, transcription, edit ops, templates), but the agent has no encoded recipe for chaining them and the app cannot render what comes back.

> **Correction, 2026-09-02 (Sweets).** The first draft of this issue opened with a `generate_music` MCP tool. That was the wrong layer. Chat runs the **sandbox agent** with a deliberately minimal tool set and reaches Recoup over **HTTP**, so an MCP tool would have shipped music to every surface except the chat. Decided: no new MCP tools; the chain is taught as a skill that curls the existing endpoints. See Architecture decisions.

## Goal

A user opens a chat, says "make a music video for this song" (or "…for a track about X"), and gets a finished music video back in the thread — playable inline, downloadable, rendered over real full-length audio.

Concretely, when this is done:

- **Song**: the agent generates one by curling the existing `POST /api/music` (MiniMax Music 3 via fal, workflow-polled, pass-through priced), or uses a track the account already has.
- **Visuals**: the agent drives `POST /api/content/video`, `POST /api/content/transcribe` and `PATCH /api/content` (crop / trim / overlay / mux) to build a lyric video or visualizer over that audio.
- **Surface**: the song and the video **play inside the message stream**. Today they arrive as bare hyperlinks.
- **Method**: the chain is encoded in a skill installed into every session sandbox, so the agent does not re-derive the pipeline each session.
- **Limits**: free-tier accounts are capped at 15 seconds of generated music and video; over-limit requests get a 402 carrying the upgrade link.

Palo Alto Networks paid $500 million in cash and stock to acquire Console, a two-year-old startup that uses AI agents to automate routine IT help desk tasks, according to two people with knowledge of the deal.
The companies officially announced the acquisition on Tuesday but didn’t reveal terms of the deal. Since its founding in 2024, Console has raised $29 million across two rounds: a $6.2 million seed led by Thrive Capital and a $23 million Series A co-led by DST Global and Thrive.
Before the sale, Console was valued at $157 million, according to PitchBook, delivering a rapid return for investors including SV Angel, Abstract Ventures, and notably Palo Alto Networks CEO Nikesh Arora, who participated as an angel investor. Palo Alto Networks declined to comment.
The cybersecurity giant said that it will integrate Console into Cortex, its platform that uses AI to automatically detect and neutralize threats. Console’s agentic functionality will allow security teams to investigate and resolve alerts using natural language, giving Cortex “the arms and legs to deliver autonomous security outcomes across the entire enterprise,” as Arora described in a statement.
Console was founded by Andrei Serban, coming shortly after his previous startup — code-security platform Fuzzbuzz — was acquired by Rippling. The startup, whose customers included Ramp, Flock Safety, and Scale AI, automated tasks like password resets, granted access to apps like Figma and Miro, and performed routine troubleshooting without direct human involvement.
As a startup, Console competed primarily with Serval, another ServiceNow challenger that hit a $1 billion valuation after raising a $75 million Series B round led by Sequoia last December. Serval started as an AI tech support tool and quickly expanded to provide AI assistance for human resources, legal, and finance departments. Console’s acquisition leaves Serval as the category-leader-to-watch among startups automating IT service management, one investor, who is not a backer of Serval, told TechCrunch.
Console is Palo Alto Networks’ seventh acquisition in 2026, according to PitchBook. Other VC-backed companies scooped up by the cybersecurity behemoth this year include Greylock and Lux Capital-backed observability platform Chronosphere, at a valuation of $3.35 billion, and Koi, a cyber startup backed by Battery and Team8, for $400 million.

## Confirmed live defect

A non-elevated audit on 2026-08-28 found a running, accepted protected lifecycle service and a completed qualified Ubuntu image, but the service has zero declarations/environments and its activity capability correctly reports unavailable. The normal installation also has no operational config.

The current setup composition can reconcile accepted image/profile/resource/declaration state only in the one-shot elevated child. The installed service generation has lifecycle read, lifecycle mutation, acceptance, and activity capabilities, but no distinct bounded setup/configuration capability. Consequently routine re-entry cannot admit an already accepted profile without another UAC transaction.

Creating config alone would start polling without execution. Direct ordinary-process Hyper-V calls, protected-package replacement, ACL weakening, or reusing a broader endpoint are prohibited bypasses.

Exact evidence, Microsoft primary-source constraints, and the dependency plan are committed in `docs/testing/DB-HO068-issue-360-no-elevation-operational-frontier.md` at `5952015`.

## Required design

Add a fifth, separate protected setup/configuration capability. It must:

- accept only one closed, bounded, revisioned accepted declaration subject/digest from the exact local installation/operator;
- carry no provider object/name, VM name, host path, executable, command, credential, transport detail, arbitrary environment value, or remote capability grant;
- use an explicit Windows named-pipe DACL separate from lifecycle read/mutation, activity, and acceptance;
- derive protected roots, images, resources, provider objects, and physical identities inside the protected service;
- perform image adoption, resource reconciliation, declaration CAS, and exact postcondition observation under the service identity;
- expose only neutral readiness/change/revision evidence;
- fail closed on endpoint absence, unsupported/stale service generation, record drift/replay, malformed/oversized input, foreign declarations, unavailable provider state, or ambiguous effects; and
- preserve the elevated child only for initial service installation/code refresh, not routine desired-state intake.

Linux must attach through an equivalent Unix-socket/system-service boundary without forcing identical provider internals.

## Acceptance

- [ ] An already-current protected authority can reconcile an accepted profile through ordinary setup without UAC.
- [ ] Initial install or service-code refresh still requires explicit administrator authority.
- [ ] Setup/configuration remains a separate capability from lifecycle read/mutation, activity, and acceptance.
- [ ] Exact operator/installation binding, DACL separation, closed schemas, wire bounds, CAS/replay, interruption/restart, and forged response behavior are proven.
- [ ] Ordinary code cannot select physical providers, VMs, image paths, protected roots, commands, executables, credentials, or transports.
- [ ] Endpoint/service absence remains fail-closed with no direct Hyper-V/libvirt or host-execution fallback.
- [ ] After one service refresh, ordinary setup admits the Linux profile, creates/verifies its environment through lifecycle authority, publishes routes/config last, and passes the fixed C canary and restart repeat.
- [ ] Windows uses the same neutral setup capability after its independently gated image/licensing policy is ready.
title: [Setup][Security] Reconcile accepted profiles through a distinct protected non-elevated channel

Covering issue from the 2026-09-02 architecture review of current `main` @ `71470bc7`.

This body supersedes the issue's original churn-weighted pass. That pass found one strong test-selection item, two next-touch seams, and one speculative web redesign, then inferred that the repository's production architecture had broadly converged. The operator correctly challenged the sampling: the review method starts from recent commits and large files, while #1278 and #1313 had themselves created most of the recent churn. The low yield proved convergence in those recently edited hotspots; it did **not** prove whole-repository convergence.

A blind cold-code control was therefore run before rewriting this register. Its result reverses the broad conclusion while preserving the useful original concerns: untouched production code still contains several strong correctness and ownership seams. #1278 and #1313 achieved real local deepening, but this review method cannot use falling hotspot counts as a repository-wide progress metric.

No implementation was performed. Figures and paths below were measured at the base SHA; re-measure every load-bearing claim against current main before building an item.

## Control-scan method

Three independent read-only reviewers audited disjoint territories:

| Territory | Untouched denominator | Sampled |
|---|---:|---:|
| `lib/` | 89 production Python files | 30 |
| `web/` + `harness/` | 41 tracked paths (37 text/code) | 32 text/code paths |
| `scripts/`, `nix/`, migrations, top-level production | 139 files | 34 |
| **Total** | **269** | **96** |

The control protocol was deliberately different from the original pass:

- Exclude every path touched anywhere in `936a4086..71470bc7`, not merely paths whose final diff changed. This removes the entire #1278/#1313 campaign plus concurrent recent work from consideration.
- Do not inspect #1278, #1313, #1355, project memory, or commit subjects while finding candidates.
- Do not use churn as a signal.
- Stratify across subsystems and small/medium/large modules rather than selecting only the largest files.
- Read production code first. Inspect tests only after a production candidate independently emerges, and then only the directly relevant tests.
- Have an uninvolved reviewer try to refute every claimed strong finding, distinguish a concrete bug from architectural leverage, and downgrade findings whose consequence did not survive.

The first pass produced 11 claimed strong findings. Cross-challenge retained seven as Strong, downgraded four, and narrowed two claims whose original consequence was too broad. Searches over current open and closed issues found no issue already owning the seven strong cold-code findings. #811 intersects Search Plan UI work but does not own the payload-contract or render-completion seams; #1321 may expose missing guards through mutation testing but does not own these production repairs.

This is static architecture evidence, not runtime proof. Each concrete production bug still owes the repository's normal generated-first or deterministic RED → fix → GREEN evidence, independent review, canonical-suite receipt, and deployment proof when implementation is authorized.
